text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) continues adding crown liquidity to the banking sector but it has ruled out offering funds at negative interest rates.

- The banking sector still remains illiquid as those banks who have enough state securities to use them in NBS repo tenders do not have liquidity problems while those who would need to raise theri financial sources do not have enough state papers.
- The Finance Ministry and Association of Investment Funds and Companies have opened talks on a new law on collective investment, expected to be presented to parliament next October.

- State-run Slovak Railways (ZSR) said its debts now totalled some 5.1 billion crowns, but it added that it was owed some four billion crowns by the state. ZSR has asked the government to provide state guarantee for a 5.4 bilion crown credit with a long-term maturity.

SME - Herbert Boesch, a co-chairman of the joint EU-Slovak parliamentary commitee, said a botched referendum in May on NATO membership and direct presidential elections had further weakened Slovakia's chances of being among leading contenders for EU admission.
- The main opposition parties will meet on Thursday to discuss a draft law on direct presidential elections worked out by the Party of the Democratic Left (SDL).

- The Opposition ethnic Hungarian Christian Democratic Movement (MKDH) said it would propose repeating a referendum with four questions, on NATO membership and presidential elections, as had been originally set down by President Michal Kovac in May and later declared invalid.
PRAVDA - South Korean Samsung has signed an agreement on withdraval from a joint-venture, home appliances producer Samsung-Calex.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The two major Slovak building societies, Prva Stavebna Sporitelna and VUB Wustenrot, will take the entire one-billion crown tranche of two-year state bonds which will be issued by the end of July to boost funds for housing construction.
- Some local dealers expect short-term rates on the interbank market to ease in the near future. The rates have already fallen below 20 percent from 35 percent a few days ago.
